content: 1. Ensure that isolation rooms or areas are equipped with appropriate hand-washing facilities, such as sinks with soap and water, and alcohol-based hand rubs near the point of care and room doors. 2. Post clear signage on the door of the isolation room to indicate restricted access. 3. Visitors must consult the nurse in charge before entering isolation areas. The nurse is responsible for maintaining a visitor log. 4. Maintain a roster of all staff working in isolation areas for potential outbreak investigations and contact tracing. 5. Remove all non-essential furniture from the isolation room. Any remaining furniture should be easy to clean and should not trap dirt or moisture. 6. Stock the sink area with necessary supplies for hand hygiene, including soap, paper towels, and alcohol-based hand rubs. 7. Place appropriate waste bags in bins, preferably touch-free bins, and ensure dirty bins remain inside the isolation room. 8. Provide puncture-proof containers for the disposal of sharps within the isolation room or area. 9. Minimize the patient’s personal belongings in the isolation room. Essential items such as water pitchers, cups, tissue wipes, and hygiene supplies should be kept within the patient’s reach. 10. Dedicate patient-care equipment (e.g., stethoscopes, thermometers, blood pressure cuffs) to individual patients whenever possible. If equipment must be shared, it should be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected before use with another patient. 11. Set up a trolley outside the isolation room door to hold personal protective equipment (PPE). Use a checklist to ensure all necessary equipment is available. 12. Place a container with a lid outside the door for equipment that requires disinfection or sterilization. 13. Keep adequate cleaning and disinfection supplies inside the isolation room and ensure meticulous daily cleaning of the area. 14. Install a telephone or other communication device in the isolation room to allow patients or visitors to communicate with healthcare workers (HCWs) without requiring HCWs to enter the room unnecessarily. PPE Usage Guidelines: 15. Before entering the isolation room, collect all necessary equipment and perform hand hygiene using an alcohol-based hand rub or soap and water. 16. Put on PPE in the correct order to ensure proper placement and to prevent self-contamination. The recommended order is: hand hygiene, gown, mask or respirator, eye protection, and gloves. 17. When leaving the isolation room, remove PPE in a manner that prevents contamination of the environment or other individuals. Remove the most contaminated items first, perform hand hygiene immediately after removing gloves, and discard the mask or respirator last. Handling of Deceased Bodies: 18. The body should be fully sealed in an impermeable body bag before removal from the isolation room to prevent leakage of body fluids. 19. Transfer the body to the mortuary as soon as possible after death. Properly packed bodies can be safely stored, cremated, or buried. 20. HCWs handling deceased bodies should wear disposable long-sleeved gowns (waterproof if body fluids are present), non-sterile gloves, and facial protection (face shield or goggles and a medical mask). Perform hand hygiene after removing PPE. Disinfectant Use: 21. Alcohol and bleach are effective disinfectants when used appropriately. Surfaces must be cleaned of organic material before applying disinfectants. 22. Ethyl alcohol (70%) is a broad-spectrum germicide effective against influenza viruses. It should be used in well-ventilated areas and only on small surface areas due to its flammability. 23. Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is effective against bacteria, fungi, and viruses, including influenza. It should be diluted appropriately and used with caution as it can irritate mucous membranes and corrode metals. Precautions for Bleach Use: 24. Always wear a mask, rubber gloves, waterproof apron, and goggles when preparing or using bleach solutions. 25. Mix bleach with cold water in well-ventilated areas, as hot water decomposes sodium hypochlorite. 26. Store bleach in a cool, shaded place, away from sunlight and out of reach of children. Prepare diluted bleach fresh daily and discard unused portions after 24 hours. PPE Stockpiling for Epidemics/Pandemics: 27. Hospitals should estimate PPE needs based on assumptions such as the frequency of HCW-patient encounters and the duration of the epidemic. 28. Medical masks should be changed between uses and whenever they become wet, damaged, or visibly soiled. 29. Respirators should be discarded after each use when caring for patients with diseases that can spread via respiratory aerosols and contact. Education and Training: 30. Educate HCWs on the safe removal, storage, handling, and reapplication of potentially contaminated equipment to minimize the risk of self-contamination and disease transmission.
